facts.subject: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system
facts.text: The control system for the Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant shall use role-based access control with named accounts for operators, engineering users, maintenance users, and read-only review users.

facts.subject: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system
facts.text: Operator privileges shall be limited to the actions needed to run assigned plant areas, and engineering privileges shall require separate approval before setpoints, control logic, alarm limits, or historian configuration are changed.

facts.subject: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system
facts.text: Remote access to the control network shall require multi-factor authentication, encrypted connectivity, a recorded business reason, and approval by the Chief Operator or Duty Engineer.

facts.label: maintains the weekly access review for maintenance accounts
disables privileges after reassignment

facts.subject: SCADA Historian Server
facts.text: The SCADA Historian Server shall be protected as a critical asset because it supports compliance review, alarm analysis, operational trending, and event reconstruction.

facts.subject: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system
facts.text: The control network shall be segmented from administrative networks, and only documented pathways shall be allowed between the SCADA Historian Server, operator workstations, controllers, and approved support systems.

facts.subject: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system
facts.text: Security patches, firmware updates, and antivirus changes shall be tested in a controlled manner before deployment to equipment that affects water production or distribution pressure.

facts.subject: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system
facts.text: Alarm priorities shall reflect consequence, response time, operator action, and the risk of losing treatment, storage, or distribution capability.

facts.subject: Chlorine Residual Alarm
facts.text: A Chlorine Residual Alarm shall remain configured as a high-priority condition when residual concentration indicates a potential treatment compliance or public health concern.

facts.subject: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system
facts.text: Alarm shelving, suppression, and disabling shall require a documented reason, a time limit, and review at the end of the operating shift.

facts.subject: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system
facts.text: Standing alarms shall be reviewed during each shift turnover so that unresolved equipment failures are not hidden by routine acknowledgement.

facts.subject: Storm Intake Mode
facts.text: During Storm Intake Mode, alarm response expectations shall account for higher debris load, faster raw water quality changes, and increased dependence on intake screening and chemical dose verification.

facts.subject: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system
facts.text: Backup power shall support safe operation or controlled shutdown of the River Intake Pump Station, Raw Water Screen Channel, Chlorine Contact Basin, Clearwell Level Controller, SCADA Historian Server, High Service Pump Header, and essential control-room equipment.

facts.subject: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system
facts.text: The plant shall maintain written expectations for generator start time, automatic transfer performance, fuel availability, and operator checks during extended utility outages.

facts.subject: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system
facts.text: Uninterruptible power supplies shall be sized to bridge transfer events and allow orderly shutdown of servers, network switches, control processors, and communication equipment.

facts.subject: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system
facts.text: Loss of both normal and standby power to a critical service shall be treated as an emergency operating condition requiring immediate notification of the Chief Operator and Duty Engineer.

facts.subject: Duty Engineer
facts.text: The Duty Engineer may authorize temporary control workarounds during an emergency, but the workaround shall be logged, bounded by time or condition, and removed when normal control is restored.

facts.subject: Distribution Dispatcher
facts.text: The Distribution Dispatcher shall be informed when failures at the High Service Pump Header, North Distribution Pressure Station, or South Distribution Pressure Station may affect pressure zones or fire-flow readiness.

facts.subject: Laboratory Technician
facts.text: The Laboratory Technician shall retain access needed for sample status review and reporting, but laboratory accounts shall not allow control actions on plant equipment.

facts.subject: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system
facts.text: Reliability targets for critical plant services shall include prompt detection of failed sensors, redundant communication paths where practical, recoverable configuration backups, and periodic restoration testing.

facts.subject: Chief Operator
facts.text: After any cybersecurity event, major alarm failure, or emergency control action, the Chief Operator shall require a brief operational review that identifies the cause, affected services, corrective actions, and any needed procedure changes.

facts.subject: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system
facts.text: Commissioning shall be planned as a controlled sequence that proves each control function before the plant relies on it for normal service.

facts.subject: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system
facts.text: Each commissioning test shall have defined starting conditions, expected responses, acceptance limits, and a responsible reviewer.

facts.subject: Duty Engineer
facts.text: Before wet commissioning begins, the Duty Engineer shall confirm that temporary controls, bypasses, and manual operating instructions are understood by the affected staff.

facts.subject: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system
facts.text: Functional testing shall verify that the River Intake Pump Station, Raw Water Screen Channel, North Filter Gallery, South Filter Gallery, and Coagulant Dosing Skid respond correctly to local and supervisory commands.

facts.subject: High Service Pump Header
facts.text: During integrated testing, Juniper shall demonstrate stable pressure control through startup, lead-lag transfer, and controlled shutdown.

facts.subject: SCADA Historian Server
facts.text: The SCADA Historian Server shall be checked for correct time synchronization, tag naming, data retention, and retrieval of key commissioning trends.

facts.subject: Chlorine Contact Basin
facts.text: The Chlorine Contact Basin and Clearwell Level Controller shall be tested under representative level, flow, and residual control conditions before treated water is released for routine distribution.

facts.subject: Storm Intake Mode
facts.text: Storm Intake Mode shall be exercised in a planned drill that confirms operator prompts, intake constraints, and return-to-normal steps.

facts.subject: Chlorine Residual Alarm
facts.text: A Chlorine Residual Alarm test shall verify annunciation, operator response guidance, acknowledgement behavior, and escalation to the appropriate duty staff.

facts.subject: Chief Operator
facts.text: The Chief Operator shall coordinate training so that operators understand the control concept, normal sequencing, manual fallback methods, and alarm response expectations.

facts.subject: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system
facts.text: Operator training shall include classroom review, simulator or dry-run practice where practical, field walkdowns, and supervised operation during early service.

facts.subject: Laboratory Technician
facts.text: The Laboratory Technician shall be trained on sample timing, result entry, data review responsibilities, and communication of unusual water quality findings.

facts.subject: Maintenance Planner
facts.text: The Maintenance Planner shall review commissioning defects, recurring nuisance alarms, calibration drift, and equipment access problems before preventive maintenance intervals are finalized.

facts.subject: Maintenance Planner
facts.text: The Maintenance Planner shall use the clip to compare observed pump condition with planned inspection intervals and corrective work priorities.

facts.label: use the clip to compare observed pump condition with planned inspection intervals

facts.subject: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system
facts.text: Feedback from maintenance work orders shall be reviewed with operations so that control changes do not mask equipment degradation or create avoidable field effort.

facts.subject: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system
facts.text: Distribution readiness shall be declared only after pressure control, reservoir or clearwell constraints, communications, and emergency contact paths have been verified.

facts.subject: Distribution Dispatcher
facts.text: Falcon shall confirm that distribution readiness messages are acknowledged before any planned change in pressure zone operating status.

facts.subject: South Distribution Pressure Station
facts.text: Before distribution readiness is declared, the South Distribution Pressure Station shall use the card to confirm zone status, valve lineup, and communication checks.

facts.subject: North Distribution Pressure Station
facts.text: The North Distribution Pressure Station shall be included in readiness checks for telemetry validity, pump permissives, local alarm indication, and operator communications.

facts.subject: Residuals Hauler
facts.text: During commissioning of residuals handling, the Residuals Hauler shall use the Backwash Solids Manifest to confirm load identity, destination, and acceptance requirements.

facts.subject: Chemical Supplier Driver
facts.text: The Chemical Supplier Driver shall follow site access, unloading, verification, and communication procedures established during commissioning and confirmed during training.

facts.subject: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system
facts.text: Records generated during commissioning and early operation shall be complete enough to support troubleshooting, regulatory review, warranty claims, and future operator training.

facts.subject: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system
facts.text: Records retention shall follow municipal policy and applicable drinking water requirements, with electronic records protected against unauthorized change and accidental loss.

facts.subject: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system
facts.text: Periodic performance reviews shall compare actual plant operation with the control concept, including alarm burden, manual interventions, water quality stability, chemical use, and energy use.

facts.subject: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system
facts.text: Continuous improvement actions shall be prioritized by risk, reviewed by the Chief Operator and Duty Engineer, tested before release, and incorporated into updated procedures and training materials.
